A cold shower can temporarily help you feel more awake and refreshed during a hangover, but ` [Highlight start] it will not cure the hangover or speed up how fast your body clears alcohol [Highlight end] `.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlgEBxCJF1wPFmdI2ICNaAORXR3UGQncAw_cXHGs0Yycql9j-9xoxqt7HKUkY1J-BRJe-h3GSlbxKNXAtBb0PLfTPLF_qaJGoOEA99hCbiWs_Ta-kq3JS9kF6SmJi5iyYROAC1g7LCqfB-PuMUft8jv6vuNixnrutuQDPun8b4Iwo0oIFORJKNnsg46I7ExXa5e2q1pCJ9fU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXX5m75AmMKgYAIbBLSYoF24CQnG6sTwa9YDuYACznOpgOe1rWcrgG5HkKubmoa4EmXpiOtp8eVpo0lxgP4sIcLLnPUx_N67TDoCmGujykj3diDUAb7j-34jUX527l4a_FWYw)

### What a Cold Shower Can Do

- **Boost alertness:** Cold water triggers a brief surge of adrenaline and endorphins, helping cut through grogginess and brain fog.
- **Improve circulation:** The temperature shift can temporarily increase blood flow and refresh your senses.
- **Offer short-term relief:** Any energizing or soothing effect is usually brief because it does not fix dehydration, low blood sugar, or poor sleep.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXX5m75AmMKgYAIbBLSYoF24CQnG6sTwa9YDuYACznOpgOe1rWcrgG5HkKubmoa4EmXpiOtp8eVpo0lxgP4sIcLLnPUx_N67TDoCmGujykj3diDUAb7j-34jUX527l4a_FWYw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlgEBxCJF1wPFmdI2ICNaAORXR3UGQncAw_cXHGs0Yycql9j-9xoxqt7HKUkY1J-BRJe-h3GSlbxKNXAtBb0PLfTPLF_qaJGoOEA99hCbiWs_Ta-kq3JS9kF6SmJi5iyYROAC1g7LCqfB-PuMUft8jv6vuNixnrutuQDPun8b4Iwo0oIFORJKNnsg46I7ExXa5e2q1pCJ9fU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF1yBaDJj9DHyyCpsMur1gL2GQ8O6yw_5Y_6yCoyIbz0eJiPkUikG1Ok4AJPwBurTCYhF5jQhHFr2lU-IotYuiv3b9Aucq1VeB3vvCe9znFRyKCc5p34VRrlpF_m_F297nKmSkQaOt3c25G4ZD_0ugBvaEK36haxi0QEby0Q)

### What It Cannot Do

- **Speed up sobriety:** Your liver breaks down alcohol at its own steady pace; cold water does not lower blood alcohol levels.
- **Cure a hangover:** There is no proven cure for a hangover—time, fluids, rest, and easy-to-digest food do the actual recovery work.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX9mh0z99WK8ZO5bYvJZPSrr1O3jp-Z3QykBn8cJOzLMRV4ul40Z5q8QNT9iJriYKs3_ilDESrRvGT1E0Q9RuqrEDzryMDJo9or4YxaJxsUoGCf_-Yc4A17PUhquRBfiWy4a9ukpnR-eKrEntaCVFew9B3gw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXX5m75AmMKgYAIbBLSYoF24CQnG6sTwa9YDuYACznOpgOe1rWcrgG5HkKubmoa4EmXpiOtp8eVpo0lxgP4sIcLLnPUx_N67TDoCmGujykj3diDUAb7j-34jUX527l4a_FWYw)

### Safety Tips

- **Wait until you are sober:** Alcohol affects how your body regulates temperature. Taking a cold shower while still intoxicated increases the risk of cold shock or hypothermia.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXo6-yDT31gX7Q2WmYECLocFo_0IkXZKW3vP0YEpYbd5xc6woG6Ey4Yzv6nEZxOQXy1xVTaXTzDdTG6Bch320NgLcv2gDsinzOxrtd2_zqr7WKho-YRSNdZB9262Z7kR-Z9Jv8Qp8Mwu5Wbr51AwsySyDuCA)
- **Keep it brief:** If you try a cold shower, keep it short (around 1 to 3 minutes) and stop if you feel dizzy, shivery, or unwell. A warm shower may be a gentler option if you want muscle relaxation instead.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXo6-yDT31gX7Q2WmYECLocFo_0IkXZKW3vP0YEpYbd5xc6woG6Ey4Yzv6nEZxOQXy1xVTaXTzDdTG6Bch320NgLcv2gDsinzOxrtd2_zqr7WKho-YRSNdZB9262Z7kR-Z9Jv8Qp8Mwu5Wbr51AwsySyDuCA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXHq7hfXAdUOSlD42GWO9UD3_HXMcNOqKQ8mx1wTt828g4aeHiETMuE_We9WPx9phoSKqE0p_1owEm3bHuOsexNdNEB0Qp9wTiDLViKExkHV9wf2lGox2uK82AnhKlmVYmVX5OhxUU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESsAEBxCJF1x2Syp8zBomy6hYt5SC1wp3cvhSzrTfZoIOKJ_m28nFPW6IyKSbBFKeM9cz3XkIW7Ix-UsebpjF-oNfXzTE2Q2aptgHzTZUVfXqmYDIKcxhxmRefu5yaLL2d-C4tUCrEMrub6CR6XbTrQwVHGQ90RcTFhQkQ1Iajpk2Q8Jo8BFHmtIMHSnqzrXGTPsNRKIrHuxn5u7GxxFWuVENwovWIbYpjLU74nAzJ7bihZA)
